solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brief union

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, short and concise in expression
an agreement or treaty binding two parties

explanation.surface: A short-lived marriage or alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a union of parties, and concise writing is called tight or brief; both senses share the one word.

clue.text: Leader fit to stop first son

indicators.note: a stopper goes into a bottle's neck, so one word is plugged into the other

parts.note: Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve
fit means apt, suitable

explanation.surface: A chief who is well suited to blocking the eldest boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's master or team skipper is the person who leads the crew or side.

clue.text: Short drink, certain to be of specified size

indicators.note: a short word has lost its final letter

parts.note: mead is a drink brewed from honey
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A small tot of spirits, guaranteed to be the stated quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short drink' looks like a tot of spirits, but 'Short' docks the last letter of MEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that measures two metres has those stated dimensions; the verb means having a given extent.

clue.text: Contents of upset muscadet cask produced an effect

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset word is turned upside down, so read from the bottom
the contents lie inside the words muscadet cask, not counting their outer letters

explanation.surface: What is inside a knocked-over barrel of white wine had consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' picks DETCA from the inside of 'muscadet cask'; 'upset' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that worked or a policy that took hold is said to have functioned or taken effect.

clue.text: Doubtfully ethical, involving separate new chapter requiring special knowledge

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the chapter letter goes inside the word built so far
separate says the two inserted letters go in apart, so the first letter goes in on its own
something doubtfully done is not reliably arranged, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dubiously moral matter, with a fresh chapter needing expert understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubtfully' rearranges ETHICAL as TECHIAL; N goes in after the H and C after the I, one each, hence 'separate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon-heavy or specialist matters need expertise; a specialised subject is described this way.

clue.text: Clumsy homeopaths dropping the prepared cleansing liquid

indicators.note: clumsy handling messes the letters of homeopaths into a new order
dropping says the letters of the word the are left out of the mix

parts.note: used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: Awkward practitioners of alternative medicine leave out the ready-mixed wash.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, H and E from HOMEOPATHS and rearrange the remaining OMOPAHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair wash is a manufactured soapy fluid sold ready-made for cleaning hair.

clue.text: Grunting sound of shattered prophet quitting Hamlet's castle

indicators.note: a shattered thing is in pieces, so its letters leave from scattered places
a person quitting a place leaves it, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Elsinore is the castle in Shakespeare's Hamlet
Eli is the Old Testament prophet-priest who taught Samuel

explanation.surface: A broken seer leaves the Danish prince's fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: E, L and I are taken from separate places in ELSINORE, which is why the prophet is 'shattered'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper's noisy, rasping breathing is a grunting kind of noise.

clue.text: Attractive area, very quiet venue of film studio

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet
Ealing, in west London, is home to the famous Ealing Studios

explanation.surface: A charming district, hushed, where films are made.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Studios, in a London suburb, made classic British comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attractive has appeal and draws people in; the adjective is a close synonym.

clue.text: Estimate consequence of ancient Briton consuming Chianti, say

indicators.note: one consuming a drink takes it inside, so the wine goes within

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain
Chianti is an example of red wine

explanation.surface: Guess the result of an early inhabitant drinking Tuscan wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to estimate what will result from something before it happens.

clue.text: Indecent fuss in support of former pupil

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
making a scene is causing a fuss

explanation.surface: A rude commotion backing an old boy of the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd or offensive material is described as indecent, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Synthetic, mouldable material; it's making a comeback in building, mostly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
mostly means most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a place can be a building, as in a place of worship

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters of it's are read backwards

explanation.surface: Artificial modelling stuff returning to construction work, by and large.
explanation.definitionFit: Polymers moulded into shapes are man-made, so the material is synthetic and pliable when heated.

clue.text: Fliers love victims on board

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: on board conventionally means inside SS, the steamship

parts.note: with on, board points to a ship, SS
prey are victims of a predator

explanation.surface: Pilots love the casualties on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the crossword convention for putting letters inside SS, steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: These fish-eating raptors are birds, and birds are things that fly.

clue.text: Nine tricks of a rabbit mating display?

parts.note: bun or bunny is a pet name for a rabbit
many birds dance as a courtship display

explanation.surface: A rabbit's courtship routine described in card-playing terms.
explanation.walkthrough: In solo whist, this is a bid to win nine of the thirteen tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: In solo whist, a declarer bidding nine tricks makes the call of this name.

clue.text: Aides working privately

indicators.note: letters at work are put into action in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Assistants doing their jobs behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark spoken apart, out of others' hearing, is made in confidence.

clue.text: Requires massages, it's said

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a masseur kneads, massages, the muscles

explanation.surface: Someone apparently has to have a rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To require something is to have to have it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cunningly nested gem cleaved into sections

indicators.note: done cunningly means artfully rearranged

explanation.surface: A jewel set in a nest was cleverly cut into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something divided into parts, like an orange, consists of segments.

clue.text: Delegated group to reach around a little bit over time

indicators.note: around says the first word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to come to a place is to reach it

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the small bit encloses the letter for time

parts.note: a mite is a tiny piece

explanation.surface: A deputed panel set to reach around a small piece in overtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel to which powers are delegated by a larger body is a working group of members.

clue.text: Remedies of powerful Italian family head cut back

parts.note: the Medici ruled Renaissance Florence

indicators.note: cut back means its tail is docked, losing the final letter

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: The cures of a Florentine dynasty whose leader was trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is not a leader but a headland: NESS, docked by 'cut back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs and treatments used to cure illness are remedies.

clue.text: Leader of tour intercepting hapless laggers who'd ultimately wandered from group

indicators.note: intercepting means getting in among, so the letter goes inside
hapless means unlucky and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the leader is the first letter of tour
ultimately means finally, the last letter of who'd

explanation.surface: A tour guide catching unlucky slowcoaches who had drifted from the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hapless' rearranges LAGGERS to SRAGGLE; 'intercepting' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stragglers trail behind or drift away from the main body of people.

clue.text: Jumps up to find what might be after Alice?

definitions.meaning: Alice ... is a town in central Australia

explanation.surface: Leaps in search of what follows a girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice Springs is a town in Australia's Northern Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap suddenly upward is to bound; the plural verb follows the town name Alice too.

clue.text: Fugitive freezes, regularly skirting smoky atmosphere on end of ridge

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge, so these letters wrap round the next piece
regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere

indicators.note: the end of ridge is its last letter

explanation.surface: A runaway shivers in a haze at the edge of a mountain ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'freezes'; FUG is a British word for a stuffy, smoky room atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fleeing persecution or war is an escapee seeking asylum.

clue.text: Framework we're filling involving new drudgery

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the crossword grid is the framework the solver fills

explanation.surface: The puzzle lattice we complete involves fresh tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotonous hard work is a daily slog; the noun means tedious toil.

clue.text: First language one recalled going round Italy

indicators.note: going round means enclosing the letter for Italy
called back, so the letters are taken in reverse

parts.note: Latin is a classical language
I is the Roman numeral one
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An old tongue brought back circles Italy first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns LATIN plus I into INITAL; 'going round' places Italy's I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at the beginning, like an opening stage, is the earliest or first one.

clue.text: Lusted-after teacher caught in act

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside the next word

parts.note: a deed is an act
sir is what pupils call a male teacher

explanation.surface: A coveted schoolmaster caught in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something craved or longed for is wanted; lust implies strong wanting.

clue.text: Put out about female getting sack

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps around the letter

parts.note: to rile is to annoy, put out

explanation.surface: An irritated woman losing her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like dismissal; here it is the verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack or plunder a place is to sack it, as an army rifles a town.

clue.text: Grease-monkeys in disastrous mischance

indicators.note: a disastrous event leaves things wrecked and reordered

explanation.surface: Car repairers caught up in a calamitous accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease-monkey is slang for a mechanic who works on engines.

clue.text: Head of corporation's serious, undergoing change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, which is replaced by another

parts.note: major means serious, as in a major problem

explanation.surface: The chief executive is grave and has had a rethink.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle J of MAJOR becomes Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A town or city corporation is headed by its elected civic leader.

clue.text: Boxer on day of victory demonstrating chi?

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight boxer
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: A fighter on a triumphant day shows his inner energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the vital life force in Chinese thought, so showing it means being living.

clue.text: When owls fly in a gallant manner, we're told

indicators.note: told means spoken to us, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: a knight acts gallantly, so knightly means chivalrously

explanation.surface: Chivalrous birds take wing after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls hunt after dark, every evening, so their flights happen each night.

clue.text: Most important person is turning to face the Queen, becoming louder?

parts.note: number one, written NO I, is the most important person

indicators.note: turning means the letters of is face the other way

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The VIP turns to address the monarch and grows more vocal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most important person' is number one, written NO + I.
explanation.definitionFit: A louder sound makes more din; the comparative of a word for rowdy.

clue.text: Barely sufficient society, principally one advancing cash

indicators.note: principally means at the start, the first letter of society

parts.note: a lender advances money

explanation.surface: Mainly society people lending money only just scrape by.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim means meagre, as in slim chances or a scant margin, scarcely enough.

clue.text: Suspected pirate died having penned lines

indicators.note: penning is shutting inside, so the pirate encloses the lines

parts.note: Smee is Captain Hook's pirate bosun in Peter Pan
L is a line, LL lines

explanation.surface: A buccaneer who wrote some verses before dying was under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is to suspect; sensed or scented something wrong.
